literal.prompt: Какое арктическое море непосредственно лежит к северу от Берингова пролива?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PMEL L18 defines the Bering Strait as southern boundary of the Chukchi shelf extending northward. This directly answers which Arctic sea is immediately north. The alternative labels are real Arctic seas, but Kara and Laptev are different Siberian receiving seas and Beaufort is distinct from the Chukchi supply sea in AFSC L82-L83. The unique key2 follows geography, not the frozen index.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: PMEL L18 identifies Chukchi and Bering Strait as its primary inflow source, and L19 says Pacific inflow provides heat and nutrients through Chukchi shelf. Both explanation sentences match. No comparative temperature, permanent direction or study-period numerical transport is added.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Карское море принимает сток Оби и Енисея.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NASA Kara L267 names Ob and Yenisei; L268 explicitly places their discharging sediment/organic material in Kara Sea. Receiving their runoff is a correctly scoped concrete fact about this distractor, rather than the queried strait adjacency.

NASA Lena L266 explicitly says the river discharges freshwater and suspended sediment into Laptev Sea. The short note accurately preserves this river-to-sea relation; it makes no ice-production claim and does not answer which sea borders Bering Strait.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Шельф Чукотского моря мелководный: на большей его части глубины меньше 50 метров.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: AFSC L82 says Chukchi shelf is shallow and predominantly less than 50m deep. The note correctly restricts the depth statement to most of its shelf, not all of the sea or its maximum depth. This is independent bathymetry beyond the whole prompt/key adjacency.

AFSC L83 specifically lists river discharge from Mackenzie among Beaufort oceanography’s three inputs. The note is the precise receiving-river statement, with no additional north-of-Alaska/Canada claim requiring other geography evidence.

absoluteLevel.ground: A thematic Arctic-map fact: identify the sea on the northern side of Bering Strait among four real Arctic seas. Adults familiar with polar geography are likely to know it; a general adult may know Bering Strait without knowing which Arctic marginal sea lies north. No obscure depth measurement is required to answer; that measurement belongs only to the supplementary note.

correctNoteExtraFact.fact: Most of Chukchi continental shelf is shallower than 50 metres.
correctNoteExtraFact.beyondWholePromptAndKey: The prompt/key gives sea/strait north adjacency; it gives no depth or shelf morphology. The note adds the named sea’s bathymetry, avoiding mere Bering connection restatement.

taxonomy.ground: Approved polar physical geography: Arctic marginal sea at the Bering gateway, with oceanographic/hydrologic own notes. It is not general climate theory, an animal fact or expedition history.
